trust_decision.summary: The rule is that server- and client-supplied sensitive values (object data, JSON schemas, task summaries/links, event sink config/routing/claim tokens, import graphs, export payloads, plaintext passwords, URL query values and server error messages) must not appear in the default diagnostic channels - Display, Debug and the std::error::Error::source chain - of any public type or error; it is decided per format implementation in the errors module, the shared client helpers and every public type, so it is many sinks with one policy, not one sink.

landing_point.why: "Default diagnostics" for a client library is what an error or a returned value prints without the caller asking for detail: the ApiError enum's thiserror Display strings and its hand-written Debug impl. It is the one place every public call funnels through, and it already has a partial redaction pattern (url and body) that a reader would extend first; the fix diff also edits this file first.

fix_sites.entry_point: every public client call that returns ApiError (Client::request_*, client.raw(...))
fix_sites.module_kind: error type: thiserror Display strings + source attributes

fix_sites.entry_point: Debug formatting of ApiError for all variants
all buffered calls via process_transport_response / parse_response
redacted_url_for_log, used by request logging and ApiError diagnostics
blocking auth_providers(), login(), login_with_token(), healthz(), readyz()

fix_sites.module_kind: resource wrapper over a request-body struct

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The resource structs (Object with `data`, Class with `json_schema`) are generated by the ApiResource proc macro in a separate package and inherit `#[derive(Debug)]` rather than writing it, and their payloads are only obtained by an explicit typed fetch - so a solver argues generated scaffolding and explicitly requested response data sit outside a diagnostics fix. The same argument covers every O8 route: the release notes say explicit response APIs keep their details.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The explicit inspection APIs must keep returning the real values: ApiError::api_message(), response_body(), request_url() and api_response() are asserted against the live payload at the pinned commit, and ImportRequest/ImportObjectInput must still Serialize the real graph so imports work. A fix that redacts where the value is stored (or deletes the Debug derive from a public type and loses the field) silently breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: three diagnostic channels that must each be closed: Display string, Debug output, and the std::error::Error::source chain
Option-wrapped sensitive value (Some/None) versus a required non-optional field
structured JSON payload (object data, json_schema, sink config, subscription routing) versus plain scalar string (password, task summary, claim token, server message)
collection of payloads (export items, export warnings, import changes, task links) versus one scalar
sensitive value carried inside a URL query string (HttpWithBody.url, reqwest::Error url, retry-error text) versus a value carried in the response body
serde decode-failure detail produced from an untrusted payload (serde_path_to_error message)
both transports: built-in reqwest and a caller-supplied AsyncTransport/BlockingTransport
